title: Operations manifest
description: shared/operations.json: what an agent can do with a hypervideo, defined once for the interpreter (client/ops/) and the chat panel's tools. Written in the subset of JSON Schema that FrameTrailSchema implements (FrameTrail's docs/DATA-MODEL.md, Schema Subset), like the input and output schemas it contains.

$defs.description: Schemas the operations' input and output schemas share, referred to as "#/$defs/<name>". Names contain no "-".

name.description: The operation's name, also the tool name agents call.

description.description: What it does, written for a model choosing a tool.

kind.description: What it reads or changes. items: overlays, annotations, chapters and code snippets.

effect.description: Whether it changes anything. Only write operations go into changesets.

scope.description: instance: the installation (no hypervideo). hypervideo: one hypervideo, which surfaces that serve several let the caller name.

preconditions.description: What must hold before it runs, checked in this order after the input. canEditHypervideo: the user may change the hypervideo's overlays, chapters, subtitles and content views (an admin or its creator; in the editor also edit mode and no lock held by someone else); refused with notAllowed. canAnnotate: the user may add annotations and change their own; notAllowed. itemExists: the item the input's ref names exists (for annotations, one of the user's own unless the input names a creator); notFound. chapterStartFree: no other chapter starts at the input's start; invalid at /start. subtitles: the hypervideo has subtitles, in the input's lang if given; notFound.

input.description: JSON Schema of the input: an object. References to FrameTrail's schemas are absolute (https://frametrail.org/schemas/1/…), references to the manifest's $defs are "#/$defs/<name>".

output.description: JSON Schema of the result, with references as in input.
